title: Sqrt(x)
summary: For a non-negative integer x, provide the square root of x, rounded down to the nearest integer, ensuring the result is also non-negative.
statement: For a non-negative integer x, provide the square root of x, rounded down to the nearest integer, ensuring the result is also non-negative. Avoid using built-in exponent functions or operators.
constraints: Return the nonnegative floor of the square root without exponent or square-root functions in your solution.
hints: The predicate candidate squared <= x changes from true to false once.
Binary-search for the largest feasible candidate, saving it before moving right.
If middle is feasible, record it and raise the lower bound; otherwise lower the upper bound.
Comparing middle <= x // middle avoids multiplication overflow; handle middle zero separately.
editorial: Search a nonnegative interval for the last value whose square does not exceed x. When a midpoint is feasible, remember it and search higher values. Otherwise search below it. At termination the saved candidate is the floor square root. Integer division provides the comparison without floating-point rounding or exponent operations.

tests.explanation: 2 squared equals 4, so the integer square root is exactly 2.
2 squared is at most 8 but 3 squared exceeds it, so round down to 2.
